---
title: the secondary column
---

Every Basalt page has three parts: the **navbar** on the left, which folds away to a chevron in the margin until you reach for it, the **note**, and the **secondary column** on the right. Nothing floats over what you're reading; anything about the page appears in that column and goes again.

## what you hover

Hover a link to another note, like [[transclusion]] or [[diagrams#graphviz|graphviz]], and its preview appears beside the page. A link out of the garden, like [Quartz](https://quartz.jzhao.xyz), says where it goes.

Every tooltip lands there too. <abbr title="Obsidian Flavored Markdown">OFM</abbr> is an abbreviation, and <span title="anything with a title attribute: its tooltip shows in the column, not as a little native box">this sentence has a title</span>. Images say what they are:

![[card.png|a test card|320]]

## what's in the margin

On a page with footnotes or asides, the column is also the page's margin: see [[margin]].
